definitions: Sigma_diag(q), Sigma_cross(q), T(q,b), c_q as in RANK3_ROUTE_D.md (D5)-(D7), reused from rank3_cross_term_probe.py. (CC1): Sigma_cross(q) = Sigma_diag(q)/(q-1) - E(q), proved here for prime q via Dirichlet character orthogonality + Gauss-sum twisting (RANK3_CROSS_TERM_CANCELLATION.md has the derivation). (CC2): Sigma_diag(q)+Sigma_cross(q) <= q*sum_b^* T(q,b), prime q, since E(q)>=0.
verdict: (CC1) verified to floating-point precision (worst relative error 3.371e-11) at every prime q in [3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19] (q=2 is degenerate, Sigma_cross(2)=0 identically) across N in [1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000, 300000, 1000000]. Consequently (CC2) holds at every one of these rows: True. Applied naively (i.e. assuming the same identity) to composite squarefree q in [6, 10, 15], the relative error ranges over [0.542, 1.564] -- large, not floating-point noise: (CC1) does not extend to composite squarefree q as derived here. This is consistent with, and explained by, the derivation's use of Gauss-sum twisting valid only for primitive characters, which every nonprincipal character mod a prime q is and not every nonprincipal character mod a composite squarefree q is.
